Definition: Integration of CRVS data (births, deaths, marriages) into data exchange for real-time verification and service eligibility
Comments: Civil registration system is "essentially paper based with no consolidated database, decentralized" per World Bank 2023 diagnostic. Digitalization of CR services underway with ANATS, with efforts to integrate with health systems. A 2019 CRVS systems report listed Chad's national ID records as electronic but CRVS as paper-based. Under active development.
revision_notes: Original sources (2023 World Bank diagnostic) confirmed as accurate for that date but are now superseded. ANATS reports at ID4Africa 2025 (via Biometric Update, June 2025) that since 2023 the civil registration system has been operationally linked to hospitals, vaccination centres, schools, mobile units and refugee camps, with data transmitted by SMS to the national registry for validation; over 120,000 births have been registered through hospital-based registry offices and the number of digitised hospital registration points is being scaled from 97 to 600. This is real, functioning (if still expanding) cross-sector integration rather than a plan, so the score is revised upward from Planned (2) to Partially integrated (4). Not raised to Fully Integrated (5) because coverage remains partial and expansion is ongoing.
revised_comments: Chad's civil registration system, managed by the National Agency for Secure Titles (ANATS), is partially integrated with other government and service-delivery systems. Since 2023, birth registration has been linked operationally to hospitals, vaccination centres, schools, mobile enrolment units and refugee camps, with data transmitted by SMS to ANATS for validation and issuance. Hospital-based registration points are being scaled up from 97 to around 600, and campaigns have registered over 120,000 children through health facilities and 180,000 through schools since 2023. Full nationwide integration is not yet achieved: the underlying civil registry remains only partly digitised, and rural/nomadic coverage relies on mobile and manual workarounds.

Definition: Extent to which the national digital identity system is integrated with the data exchange for identity verification and authentication
Comments: In 2020, Chad introduced SIGPTS (integrated identity management system) managed by ANATS, providing unique National Identification Number (NIN) through National Biometric Registration Program (RNBP). However, two separate systems exist for civil registration (paper-based) and national ID card, requiring reforms. Integration with data exchange platform lacking. World Bank notes "existing government recognized legal identification systems require reforms to serve as foundation for digital service delivery.
revision_notes: Original World Bank sources confirmed accurate for 2023-24. Fresh check (Biometric Update, 16 March 2026) finds Chad's Ministry of Finance and ANATS signed an agreement, days before the article, to interconnect with the national biometric registry (SIGPTS) for real-time identity data sharing in administrative and financial procedures, with the stated ambition to onboard 'many' other ministries and agencies. This is a single, very recent agreement covering one ministry and described in future/aspirational terms ('aims to facilitate'), so it does not yet demonstrate operational, multi-agency integration. Score is confirmed at Under development (3) rather than upgraded, pending evidence that the interconnection is live and extended beyond Finance.
revised_comments: Chad's national biometric identity system (SIGPTS, managed by ANATS) remains under development as a foundation for cross-government data exchange. Civil registration and national ID are still managed as two only partly linked systems. In March 2026 the Ministry of Finance and ANATS signed an interoperability agreement to enable real-time consultation of biometric identity data for administrative and financial verification, with ANATS stating an ambition to bring further ministries and private-sector partners onto the registry as a single source of identity truth. Broader integration across government agencies has not yet been operationalised.

Definition: Integration of health records, patient registration, immunization data, and health insurance into data exchange
Comments: Digital clinical decision support system (TRICC) piloted in refugee/rural health contexts with NGO support. Cloud server subscription required (government infrastructure insufficient for local server). Integration of CR services with health systems mentioned in WB project. No national health information system integrated with government data exchange.
revision_notes: Sources confirmed. The PMC article (April 2025) describes a small, NGO-supported tablet-based clinical decision support pilot (2019-2023) in three primary health facilities in southern Chad, not a national health information system. Health facilities and vaccination centres are being used as intake points for birth registration under ANATS (Biometric Update, June 2025), but this is civil-registration data collection via health facilities rather than health records, immunisation or insurance data being integrated into a government data exchange. No evidence found of a national health information system or health insurance data linked to a data exchange platform, so the score is confirmed unchanged at Planned (2).
revised_comments: No national health information system in Chad is yet integrated into a government-wide data exchange. Digital health activity is limited to donor/NGO-supported pilots, such as a tablet-based clinical decision support system trialled in a small number of primary health facilities in a refugee-affected district (2019-2023), and to the use of hospitals and vaccination centres as intake points for birth registration under ANATS. Patient records, immunisation data and health insurance systems remain unintegrated with cross-government data exchange infrastructure.

Definition: Integration with national payment systems for government-to-person (G2P), government-to-business (G2B) transactions via data exchange
Comments: Digital payments infrastructure limited: "a shared government digital payments infrastructure is not available and the GoC makes limited use of digital means of payment." Some mobile money for community teachers and cash transfers. e-Tax and e-Tax modules launched from 2022 onward. Limited interoperability among mobile wallet providers.
revision_notes: Original 2023 World Bank diagnostic confirmed accurate for its date. The World Bank's Chad Digital Transformation Project Implementation Status Report (24 Aug 2025) shows the digital-payments sub-component (G2P/P2G) is now active but pre-operational: tenders for an e-procurement system and electronic payment terminals were only just initiated, and the share of people making/receiving a digital payment was flat at 18-19% between September 2024 and January 2025 (targets set for 2029). A March 2026 IFC/Cashi press release confirms a new interoperable digital-payments platform is being built for Chad, connecting banks, telecoms and other institutions, still at the market-entry stage. This shows movement beyond 'Planned' into active implementation, but no functioning shared G2P/G2B payments-data-exchange layer yet exists, so the score is revised from Planned (2) to Under development (3).
revised_comments: Chad's government digital-payments infrastructure is under development but not yet integrated into a shared data exchange. A World Bank-financed digital transformation project has initiated tenders for e-procurement and electronic payment terminals, targeting government-to-person and person-to-government digitalisation, but implementation indicators (such as the share of people making or receiving a digital payment, around 18-19%) had not moved as of early 2025. In March 2026, IFC partnered with fintech Cashi to build an interoperable digital-payments platform connecting banks, mobile money operators and other institutions, aimed at extending financial access, including for government payments, in low-connectivity areas. A common, government-wide digital-payments interoperability layer is not yet operational.

Definition: Integration of tax administration and revenue collection systems data into the exchange platform
Comments: SIGFiP (Integrated Public Finance Management System), eTax application, and ASYCUDA World (customs) are operational back-office systems. e-Tax platform launched July 2022. e-registration and new e-Tax modules launched March and May 2023. However, these systems are siloed and not integrated through a common interoperability framework.
revision_notes: Original sources confirmed accurate for 2022-23, when SIGFiP, e-Tax and ASYCUDA (Sydonia) were described as siloed. Since then, concrete interoperability steps have been reported: a Ministry of Finance document mandates interconnection obligations covering SIGFiP, e-Tax, Sydonia, e-Enregistrement, e-Conservation and e-Notaire; a January 2026 report (Le N'Djam Post) describes SIGFIP as already facilitating interoperability with Sydonia (customs) and e-Tax to produce regular consolidated financial reporting under the 'zero cash, zero paper' 2026 budget reform; and on 1 April 2026 the Directorate-General of Taxes (DGI) and the Directorate-General of Treasury and Public Accounting (DGTCP) signed a formal data-exchange protocol for automated, real-time sharing of tax assessments, collections, arrears and payments. This is evidence of an operating, if still-expanding, interoperability framework across core revenue and finance systems, so the score is revised from Under development (3) to Partially integrated (4). Not raised to Fully Integrated (5) given the DGI-DGTCP link is only weeks old and full-system rollout (e.g. e-Notaire, e-Conservation) is not yet confirmed as live.
revised_comments: Chad's core public finance and revenue systems are partially integrated. The Integrated Public Finance Management System (SIGFiP) now interoperates with the customs platform (Sydonia) and the e-Tax application to support consolidated budget execution reporting under the government's 2026 'zero cash, zero paper' reform. On 1 April 2026, the tax administration (DGI) and the treasury and public accounting directorate (DGTCP) signed a protocol establishing automated, real-time exchange of data on tax assessments, collections, arrears and payments between the two administrations, and Ministry of Finance rules require interconnection across SIGFiP, e-Tax, Sydonia, e-Registration, e-Conservation and e-Notary systems. Full integration across all listed systems, with enforcement and public reporting, is still being rolled out.
